methodology: Per-analyzer binary/multiclass scoring against labeled corpora (tests/accuracy/corpus.py). Synthetic and real corpora are reported separately and never pooled. Real labels: role bindings from prior verified analysis plus cross-labeling. Output carries role labels and counts only. no local labeling file; derived role bindings + cross-labels only

engine_identification.definition: per-family binary detection (nar-engines detected verdict in the family); negatives are cross-labeled fixtures of other families

framework_detection.definition: per-framework binary detection; negatives are cross-labeled fixtures of other frameworks

protection_attribution.definition: an attributed commercial_packer finding in nar-triage output; negatives are the clean set plus cross-labeled fixtures

synthetic.definition: nar-network classify() against construction-defined labels; measures rule consistency, weaker than independent human labeling

real.reason: no independently labeled endpoint corpus exists locally: ground truth would require hand-labeled URL classifications for real apps, and none is recorded

native_library_identification.reason: no labeled native-library corpus is recorded locally: ground truth would require per-fixture verified library inventories, and none is recorded; library lists are reported per case, unmeasured

security_finding_classification.reason: no labeled security-findings corpus exists locally: findings are deterministic rule outputs and no independent ground-truth labels (which findings SHOULD fire on which fixture) are recorded; inventing them from the rules themselves would be circular
